title: The temporal stochastic block model
summary: Motivated by the need to understand infection spreading in inhomogeneous populations, we consider a \emph{temporal} version of the stochastic block model, where each edge is equipped with a random label, interpreted as a timestamp. We study the size and structure of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing) where the connections per node are of the order of $\log n$. We prove tight results for the first order asymptotics of the size of the reachable set from a typical vertex, and the proportions of reached vertices in each community.…
